meta_title: Bucky - screen time your kids earn
meta_description: A kids video app where watching is earned in short maths and spelling lessons, and every video was approved by a parent. No ads, no autoplay, no account needed.
hero_eyebrow: A video app for kids, made by parents
hero_lead: Kids watch only the videos you approved. Every minute costs a few Popcorn Pals, and kids earn Pals in short, friendly lessons: adding, times tables and spelling. No negotiating, no tears when it's over.
fact_no_ads: No ads of its own, no autoplay
alt_bucky: Bucky, a smiling pink and mint popcorn bucket, with three little popcorn kernels floating around him
alt_shot_who: Bucky's start screen asking "Hi there! Who's playing?" with two kid profiles
promise1_text: No recommendations, no rabbit holes. Kids see your list and nothing else.
promise2_text: Watching feels like a reward for effort, and the rules feel like a game.
promise3_text: No punishing sounds, no guilt, no countdown pressure. Bucky is always on the kid's side.
how_title: Learn a little, watch a little
how_lead: Bucky is a popcorn bucket, and his popcorn is the currency. How full Bucky is shows how much watching is left, so even kids who don't read numbers yet get it.
how1_text: A few quick puzzles at the kid's own level. Wrong answers get an encouraging "Oops, try again!", never a buzzer.
how2_text: Every right answer pops Pals into Bucky. Save them up, or put them in Bucky's bank and watch them grow.
how3_text: Pick something from the family library. Each started minute costs a few Pals, and they hop out of Bucky one by one while the video plays.
how_loop: When the Pals run out, the video pauses and a short lesson starts. Finish it, and the video picks up right where it stopped. Watching ends naturally, without a fight.
lessons_lead: A parent picks which lessons each kid gets and at what level. A few minutes a day adds up to a habit.
lesson_add_text: Count popcorn, pick the answer. Levels from within 5 up to within 20, with counters for little ones who still like to count.
lesson_mul_text: Timed tables within 100, and bigger ones up to 200 with the split method: three levels of help, and more Pals for doing it alone.
lesson_dict_text: Ten grade-4 dictations. Pick the right spelling for each gap: ó or u, rz or ż, ch or h.
lesson_sub_text: Taking away popcorn, the same gentle way as adding.
alt_shot_addition: Addition lesson: 3 + 2 with popcorn counters and three big answer buttons
alt_shot_split: Times tables lesson: 19 x 6 with a number pad and a "Split it myself" help button
alt_shot_times: Times tables lesson: 7 x 8 with a number pad
alt_shot_dictation: Polish dictation lesson: a short story with gaps and two spelling options above the current gap
kids_lead: Bucky reacts to everything a kid does, and he is never cross. Sad is only ever "a little hungry".
kids1_text: Brothers and sisters share one phone or tablet. Each kid picks their profile on "Who's playing?" and has their own colour, Pals, lessons and videos.
kids2_text: Put Pals in the bank, and every night at midnight it adds a little more. Kids learn to save first and spend later, and see their savings grow.
kids3_text: While a video plays, Pals pop out of Bucky and march off the screen, one per minute. A tiny clock shows when the next one goes.
kids4_text: Chunky rounded digits, big tap targets and pictures instead of menus, for kids who are still learning to read.
alt_bank: Bucky standing in front of a little bank building with bags of popcorn
alt_shot_bank: Bucky's bank screen: "The bank gave you 2 Pals!", 7 Pals in hand and 22 in the bank at 10% a day
parents_title: Set the rules once. Then relax.
parents_lead: Parent mode sits behind a PIN. Everything is per kid, so the six-year-old and the nine-year-old each get what fits them.
approve_text: Paste a YouTube link to a single video, a playlist or a whole channel. Bucky lists what's in it, skips Shorts and live streams, and lets you filter by length and language. Choose which kids see each source.
warnings_text: Before anything is added, Bucky flags the kinds of videos many parents would rather skip, so you can hide whole kinds at once:
alt_shot_add: Add videos screen: a pasted channel link, four videos found, Shorts skipped, and content warnings for shopping hauls and blind boxes
alt_shot_settings: Kid settings screen: name, colour, lessons with addition levels, and how many Pals are needed to start watching
p_pin_text: Settings are locked behind a 4-digit PIN that kids don't know.
p_stats_text: Per kid, today and the last 7 days: watching time, lessons done, accuracy, speed and the trickiest facts.
p_breaks_text: A break with a task every 5 to 60 minutes of watching, and a closed cinema for a while afterwards.
p_price_text: Set how many Pals a kid needs before starting (10 by default) and how much a minute of each kind of video costs.
p_family_text: Invite the other parent with a short code. Several parents can manage one family.
p_sync_text: Sign in with Google or Apple and the phone and the tablet share Pals, bank, videos and settings.
p_share_text: On Android, tap Share on any YouTube video and send it straight to Bucky.
p_assign_text: Each playlist or channel is for every kid or only some of them, and new videos in it follow the same rule.
cinema_text: When it's break time, Bucky asks for a stretch and a quick task. After a break the cinema can stay closed for a while, with a friendly countdown instead of an argument. Kids can still do lessons and visit the bank while they wait.
alt_cinema: A cosy cinema at night with the lights off and Bucky sitting on the steps
alt_break: Bucky smiling next to a pause button
privacy_lead: Bucky works fully on one device without any account. Nothing leaves the device then, apart from YouTube loading the videos you approved.
stored_title: Stored, only with a family account
stored_intro: If you sign in to share a family across devices, this is kept in our Firebase project in the EU (Warsaw, Poland):
stored_1: Your sign-in id and email, to know who owns the family
stored_3: Pals, bank balance and watching-time totals
stored_4: The parent PIN, as a hash only
stored_5: The videos you added and the kinds you hid
never_intro: Some things simply never leave the device, or are never collected at all:
never_1: What a kid watched, and when
note1_text: Videos play in YouTube's own embedded player, as YouTube's terms require. Bucky doesn't block YouTube's ads and never charges for playback.
note2_text: The activity log behind the parent stats lives on the device only.
note3_text: Security rules let only members of a family read or change it. Signing out removes a device from syncing.
faq1_q: Can my kid find other videos in Bucky?
faq1_a: No. Kids only see the videos, playlists and channels a parent added. There is no search, no recommendations and no autoplay into something new.
faq2_a: No. On one device Bucky works without any account. A family account (Google or Apple sign-in) is only needed if you want the same kids, Pals and videos on several devices.
faq3_q: Which devices does it run on?
faq3_a: Android phones and tablets, and iPhone and iPad. The iPhone and iPad version is in TestFlight for now.
faq4_q: What happens when the Pals run out in the middle of a video?
faq4_a: The video pauses and a short lesson starts. When it's done, the video continues from the same moment. You decide how many Pals a kid needs to start again.
faq5_a: The lessons go from adding within 5, for kids who still count on their fingers, to times tables up to 200 and grade-4 Polish spelling. You set the level for each kid.
faq6_a: No. Videos play in YouTube's official embedded player, as YouTube's terms require, so YouTube may still show its own ads. Bucky itself shows no ads and has no in-app purchases for kids.
faq7_a: Yes. Each kid has a profile with their own Pals, bank, lessons, settings and videos, and picks it on the start screen.
faq8_a: English and Polish. Bucky follows the device language, and a parent can switch it in parent mode.
cta_text: Bucky is in early testing with a small group of families. Drop us a line and we'll let you know when there's room.
cta_small: No newsletter, no spam. Just one message when it's your turn.
